Time Quintet: Time Quintet is fantasy/science fiction series of five young adult novels written by Madeleine L'Engle.
 A Wind in the Door: Wind in the Door is young adult science fantasy novel by Madeleine L'Engle companion book to "A Wrinkle in Time", part of Time Quintet.
 Close the Last Door: Door (Japanese: 最後のドアを閉めろ! , Hepburn: Saigo no Door wo Shimero! ) yaoi manga series written by Yugi Yamada. adapted into OVA directed by Tama. licensed in North America by Digital Manga Publishing published first volume in 2006.
 Kaze Hikaru: Kaze Hikaru (Japanese: 風光る , lit. "Shining Wind") Japanese manga series written illustrated by Taeko Watanabe. Set in "bakumatsu" period series follows Tominaga Sei, young girl poses as boy Kamiya Seizaburo join Mibu-Roshi (Special Police; later known as Shinsengumi). befriends sensei, Okita Sōji, who discovers her secret.
 Kaze no Stigma: Stigma of the Wind or Kaze no Stigma (Japanese: 風の<ruby ><rb>聖痕</rb><rp> (</rp><rt >スティグマ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby> , Hepburn: Kaze no Sutiguma , lit. "Stigma of the Wind") Japanese light novel series written by Takahiro Yamato illustrated by Hanamaru Nanto. After death of author on July 20, 2009, story remains incomplete at twelve chapters. 24-episode anime adaptation directed by Junichi Sakata animated by Gonzo aired from April–September 2007. dubbed in English by Animax Asia under title Stigma of the Wind and by Funimation as Kaze no Stigma.
Four Winds of Love: Four Winds is overall title for series of six novels written by Compton Mackenzie, "The East Wind of Love" (1937), South Wind of Love" (1938), West Wind of Love" (1940), "West to North" (1942), "The North Wind of Love, Book 1" (1944) and "The North Wind of Love, Book 2" (1945), together constitute major fictional chronicle of first forty years of twentieth century main protagonist of hexalogy is semi-autobiographical character of John Ogilvie.

Rotterdam The Hague Airport: Rotterdam (formerly "Rotterdam Airport", "Vliegveld Zestienhoven" in Dutch), (IATA: RTM, ICAO: EHRD) located 3 NM north northwest of Rotterdam, is Netherlands' third largest airport serves city of Rotterdam The Hague and surroundings. airport handled over 1.6 million passengers in 2016 features scheduled flights to European metropolitan and leisure destinations. used extensively by general aviation several flying clubs and schools at airport.
 A13 motorway (Netherlands): A13 motorway is motorway in Netherlands connecting cities The Hague and Rotterdam. Rotterdam The Hague Airport next to A13.
 Lahad Datu Airport: Lahad Datu Airport (IATA: LDU, ICAO: WBKD) is airport in southeastern of Malaysian state of Sabah. airport, approximately 1 km from downtown Lahad Datu serves town of Lahad Datu and neighbouring districts Kinabatangan, FELDA Sahabat and Kunak. airport can accommodate aircraft large as ATR72 terminal building can handle up to 100,000 passengers annually. In 2016, airport handled 140,077 passengers and 3,713 aircraft movements.
 Exeter Airport: Exeter Airport (IATA: EXT, ICAO: EGTE), formerly "Exeter International Airport", airport located at Clyst Honiton in District of East Devon close to city of Exeter within county of Devon, South West England. In 2007 airport handled over 1 million passengers for first time, passenger throughput declined. In 2016 handled 847,257 passengers, a 3.1% increase compared with 2015. Exeter has CAA Public Use Aerodrome Licence (Number P759) allows flights for public transport passengers or for flying instruction. airport offers scheduled and holiday charter flights within United Kingdom and Europe.
Sofia Airport: Sofia Airport (IATA: SOF, ICAO: LBSF) (Bulgarian: Летище София, "Letishte Sofiya" ) is main international airport of Bulgaria located 10 km east from centre of capital city Sofia. In 2015 airport surpassed 4 million passengers for first time handled total of 4,088,943 passengers, a 7.2% increase compared to 3,815,158 passengers in 2014. In 2016, number rose to almost 5 million passengers. airport serves as home base for BH Air, Bulgaria Air, Bulgarian Air Charter and base for Ryanair and Wizz Air. Vrazhdebna Air Base of Bulgarian Air Force is also located at airport.
 International air travel from United Kingdom: International air travel from United Kingdom refers to commercial carriage of passengers between UK and rest of world. In 2008, London Heathrow Airport busiest international airport on handled 67,054,745 passengers more than total population of United Kingdom. 20 busiest airports in UK handled close to 230 million passengers in 2008 (185 million were international passengers). geographical size of UK means many flights domestic in are actually international (i distance from Heathrow to Charles de Gaulle Airport roughly same as distance between John F. Kennedy International Airport and Washington Dulles International Airport). London airports, Heathrow, Gatwick Stansted alongside Manchester Airport rank amongst world's busiest airports by international passenger traffic. According to 2008 statistics best served nations by direct flights from UK were France, Italy, Spain, United States Germany with 50, 34, 33, 31 and 29 respectively. Spain was nation saw most passengers arrive from UK in 2008, with total of 34,557,729 (almost double the number flew to United States)

Deeyah Khan: Deeyah Khan (Urdu: , ] , born 7 August 1977 in Oslo, Norway), is a Norwegian film director and human rights defender of Punjabi/Pashtun descent.
 Damien Dematra: Damien Dematra is an Indonesian movie director, novelist, script writer, producer, international photographer, and painter. has written 101 novels in dual languages, English and Indonesian, 81 films and TV scenarios, produced 48 films in various genres; among them is internationally distributed "Obama Anak Menteng" ('Little Obama'), the award-winning movie "Si Anak Kampoeng" ('The Village Boy'), "L4 Lupus, "the record breaking movie "Dream Obama", "I'M STAR", "Let's Play, Ghost", "Dorce Vs. Hantu", and documentary film: "Gus Dur the Final Year", "Obama and Me"," Captain Jihad".
 Sandi Simcha DuBowski: Sandi Simcha DuBowski is an American director and producer, best known for his work on the intersection of LGBT people and their religion, DuBowski directed 2001 documentary "Trembling Before G-d" the producer of Parvez Sharma's documentary "A Jihad for Love" (formerly known as "In the Name of Allah") (2007).
 A Sinner in Mecca: A Sinner in Mecca is a 2015 documentary film from director Parvez Sharma ("A Jihad for Love"). film chronicles Sharma's Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca, Saudi Arabia as an openly gay Muslim. film premiered at the 2015 Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival to great critical acclaim. film opened in theaters in the US on September 4, 2015 is a New York Times Critics' Pick.
 Steven Stalinsky: Steven Stalinsky is an expert on Middle East, terrorism and terrorist use of Internet, and encryption technologies, served as Executive Director of the Middle East Media Research Institute (MEMRI) since 1999. Stalinsky has briefed staff of the White House, State Department, Homeland Security, Justice Department, Office of Director of National Intelligence, Defense Department, Capitol Hill and other institutions.Since 2006, his research has focused on detailing and developing strategies against cyber jihad, describing how terrorist groups such as Al-Qaeda, ISIS, and others use Internet, social media, and encryption for propaganda, recruiting, and hacking. He was early advocate of calling on tech community to take stronger action on removing terrorist content from their platforms and for creating industry standards to combat it.
 A Jihad for Love: A Jihad for Love (also known by working title In the Name of Allah) is a 2007 documentary film on the coexistence of Islam and homosexuality. film is directed by Parvez Sharma, produced by Sharma and "Trembling Before G-d" director Sandi DuBowski.
 Jihad: A Story of the Others: JIHAD: a story of the others is a 2015 documentary film by Emmy and Peabody Award winning Norwegian director Deeyah Khan. film is produced by Khan's production company Fuuse. "JIHAD" is the outcome of a two-year investigation by Deeyah and provides a view from inside about what it is like to be drawn into radicalism. documentary film sets out to provide insight into why some young Muslims in the West embrace violent extremism and go abroad to fight holy wars and in some cases why they came to reject it.

LECOM Park: LECOM Park is a baseball field in Bradenton, Florida spring training home of Pittsburgh Pirates named after 15-year naming rights deal signed with Lake Erie College of Osteopathic Medicine, main campus in Erie, Pennsylvania and also campus in Bradenton. Formerly known as McKechnie Field named for Bradenton resident and baseball great Bill McKechnie, led Pirates in 1925 and Cincinnati Reds in 1940 to World Series titles. was coach of Cleveland Indians in 1948. notable members of Baseball Hall of Fame Roberto Clemente, Willie Stargell, Bill Mazeroski, Babe Ruth Ted Williams Mike Schmidt, played at LECOM Park. stadium hosts minor league baseball games for Bradenton Marauders, Pirates' High-A club in Florida State League.
 Athletics Stadium: Athletics Stadium is a former minor league baseball stadium in Tulsa, Oklahoma. stadium known as Drillers Stadium until early 2014 adopted current name. From 1981 to 2009, Drillers Stadium was home to Tulsa Drillers, of Double-A Texas League. For Drillers Stadium hosted regular season baseball games between Oklahoma State University and University of Oklahoma in Bedlam Series.
 Dr Pepper Ballpark: Dr Pepper Ballpark (formerly Dr Pepper/Seven Up Ballpark) is home ballpark of Frisco RoughRiders Class AA minor league baseball club. Located in Frisco, Texas United States stadium has capacity of 10,316. ballpark is host to numerous functions minor league baseball games, including corporate and charity events, wedding receptions, city of Frisco events, church services. Local soft drink manufacturer Dr Pepper Snapple Group holds naming rights and exclusive non-alcoholic beverage rights in park.
 Newark Bears (International League): Newark Bears were a Minor League Baseball team in International League, beginning in 1917 at Double-A level.played in International League through 1949 season, except for 1920 and part of 1925 season. Bears' last four seasons in International League (1946–1949), were a Triple-A team, highest classification in minor league baseball played home games at Ruppert Stadium in now known as Ironbound section of Newark; stadium demolished in 1967 1932, 1937, 1938, and 1941 Bears recognized as among 100 greatest minor league teams of all time.
 Josh Holliday: Josh Holliday (born September 14, 1976) is American college baseball coach and former professional player in Minor League Baseball. Currently head coach of Oklahoma State Cowboys baseball team, hired to this position prior to 2013 season. In 2014, Holliday was Big 12 Conference Baseball Coach of the Year as OSU claimed conference regular season championship. Hollidays' Cowboys pulled OSU Cowboy baseball tradition out of fire faced Oklahoma on final weekend of 2017. team in danger of missing out of postseason for 1st time in Hollidays tenure at Oklahoma State. Cowboys swept instate rival Oklahoma Sooners (#2 seed going into region play) to claim last and final spot as 8th seed in BigXII Championship. Cowboys went back to traditionion won 2nd Big 12 tournament in schools rich baseball history. Cowboys won 16 straight Big 8 tournaments before formation of Big12. Cowboys became 1st eight seed (last seed) to win conference championship Holliday got his team in NCAA postseason for 5th time in his 5 years at school season was full of injuries from top to bottom Holliday and associated Head Coach and current (2016) assistant coach of the year Rob Walton put together pitching staff of magical. Cowboys luck run out sent to Arkansas Regional and went 0-2 losing game one to Regional champions Missouri State Bears on two out bottom of 9th walk off HR.Garrett Benge hit for cycle for Hollidays Cowboys wasn't enough. Garrett McCain named 1st team all-American 25th in Cowboys history one of five current Cowboys drafted in 2017 preceded by 11 from 2016 College World Series club. Giving Holliday 16 in 2 years. Cowboys went on end of year run seen lose six games in a row face 1st Oklahoma State team to finish under .500 in 40 years.The Cowboys finished 30-27 on year. 6-5 victory of Texas Longhorns Hollidays' 200th victory as head man of Oklahoma State.

Gainesville, Florida: Gainesville is county seat and largest city in Alachua County, Florida, United States, and principal city of the Gainesville, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA). population of Gainesville in 2013 US Census estimates was 127,488, a 2.4% growth from 2010. Gainesville is the largest city in region of North Central Florida. also a component of the Gainesville-Lake City Combined Statistical Area, had a 2013 population of 337,925.
 Cooperative Living Organization: Cooperative Living Organization (formerly Collegiate Living Organization) or CLO in Gainesville, Florida, is one of oldest continuously operating independent student-governed cooperative living organizations in United States. 80-year-old organization has provided over 2000 financially disadvantaged students opportunity for University of Florida education while providing experience in independent and socially responsible living by pooled resources and self-governance.
 Florida's 16th congressional district: Florida's 16th congressional district is an electoral district for the U.S. Congress was reassigned in 2012, effective January 2013, to western Manatee County, Florida and Sarasota County. district stretches from Bradenton, County Seat, in Manatee County to North Port, in Sarasota County, the county's youngest and most populous incorporated city. city of Sarasota is the County Seat of Sarasota County.
 Mason, Michigan: Mason is a city in U.S. state of Michigan. named after state's first governor, Stevens T. Mason. As of 2010 census, city population was 8,252. It is county seat of Ingham County. Mason is the only city in U.S. that serves as a county seat ahead of a state capital, with the capital of Lansing also in Ingham County. Despite Mason being county seat, many county offices and courtrooms are located in Lansing.
 Tampa–Hillsborough County Public Library System: The Tampa–Hillsborough County Public Library System (THPL) is a public library system based in Hillsborough County, Florida.State Library of Florida is main library source for Government of Florida governs a large portion of Florida's public and private libraries. THPL is part of two larger library networks, Hillsborough County Public Library Cooperative and Tampa Bay Library Consortium, also includes Temple Terrace Public Library in Temple Terrace, Florida, and Bruton Memorial Library in Plant City, Florida. are 25 branches of the Tampa–Hillsborough County Library System, not including digital-only and mobile-only services. Services provided by THPL include (but in no limited to) internet access, public meeting room spaces, interlibrary loans, a Bookmobile, a Cybermobile for Spanish speakers, technology classes, adult literacy programs, and downloadable eBooks. Drive-thru windows for returns and hold pick-ups are located at the Jimmie B. Keel and Jan Kaminis Platt Regional Libraries. Tampa–Hillsborough County Public Library System is also a part of Hillsborough County government.
 Cumberland Homesteads: Cumberland Homesteads is a community located in Cumberland County, Tennessee, United States. Established by the New Deal-era Division of Subsistence Homesteads in 1934, community was envisioned by federal planners as a model of cooperative living for the region's distressed farmers, coal miners, and factory workers. While cooperative experiment failed and federal government withdrew from the project in the 1940s, Homesteads community nevertheless survived. In 1988, several hundred of community's original houses and other buildings, characterized by native "crab orchard" sandstone used in their construction, were added to the National Register of Historic Places as a historic district.

Fortress Series: Fortress is series of fantasy novels by science fiction fantasy author C. J. Cherryh published by HarperCollins. set in medieval fantasy world with 15th-century feel feature magic, sorcery, medieval warfare, politics other elements common to high fantasy subgenre. first book series, "Fortress in Eye of Time", published in 1995 followed by "Fortress of Eagles" in 1998, "Fortress of Owls" in 1999 "Fortress of Dragons" in 2000 "Fortress of Ice" in 2006.
 Pen name: A pen name ("nom de plume", or "literary double") is a pseudonym (or, variant form of real name) adopted by author printed on title page or by-line of works in place of "real" name. pen name may be used to make author's name distinctive disguise gender distance author from previous works protect author from retribution for writings combine more than one author into single author or for reasons related to marketing or aesthetic presentation of work. author's name may be known only to publisher, or may be common knowledge.
 C. J. Cherryh: Carolyn Janice Cherry (born September 1, 1942), better known by pen name C. J. Cherryh, is American writer of speculative fiction. written more than 60 books since mid-1970s, including Hugo Award-winning novels "Downbelow Station" (1981) and "Cyteen" (1988), both set in Alliance-Union universe. known for "world building," depicting fictional realms with great realism supported by research in history, language, psychology, archeology. Her series of fantasy novels set in Alliance-Union universe, Morgaine Stories, sold in excess of 3 million copies.
Lionel Snell: Ramsey Dukes is current well-known pen name of Lionel Snell, contemporary English magician, publisher author on magic philosophy. has also pen names Lemuel Johnston. Angerford and Lea, Adamai Philotunus Per Anum Ad Astra. His regular satirical column "The Satanist's Diary" published in magazine "Aquarian Arrow" during 1980s early 1990s under pen name The Hon Hugo C StJ l'Estrange included other pen names contributors.
 Jane Thayer: Jane Thayer (the pen name of Catherine Woolley, August 11, 1904 – July 23, 2005) was American writer. known best for book "The Puppy Who Wanted A Boy", basis of 1980s Saturday Morning cartoon series, "The Puppy's Further Adventures". Jane Thayer wrote 86 books for children many ("The Blueberry Pie Elf" "The Puppy Who Wanted a Boy for Christmas") become classics. prolific editor suggested publish works under pen name Catherine authored picture books under pen name Jane Thayer writing books for older children adults under real name.

Segugio Italiano: Segugio Italiano ] is an Italian breed of dog of the scenthound family. It comes in both short-haired and wire-haired varieties. It thought to be an ancient breed, descended in pre-Roman eras from progenitor scenthounds in ancient Egypt. In 2009 ENCI (the Italian Kennel Club) registered 4,500 specimens of short-haired variety and 1,740 wire-haired specimens, making this one of top ten breeds in Italy.
 Sapsali: The Sapsali (삽살이) is a shaggy Korean breed of dog. word is followed in Korean by either "gae" (meaning "dog") or suffix "ee"/"i", but most commonly romanized as "Sapsaree". Traditionally, these dogs were believed to dispel ghosts and evil spirits.
 Shisa: Shisa (シーサー , Shīsā , Okinawan: "shiisaa") is a traditional Ryukyuan cultural artifact and decoration, often seen in similar pairs, resembling a cross between a lion and a dog, from Okinawan mythology. In magic typology, they sometimes also be classified as gargoyle beasts. Shisa are wards, believed to protect from some evils. People place pairs of shisa on rooftops or flanking the gates to houses, with left shisa has a closed mouth, right one an open mouth. open mouth wards off evil spirits, closed mouth keeps good spirits in.
 Ba-Jia-Jiang: Ba Jia Jiang (八家將) originated from the Chinese folk beliefs and myths, usually refers to eight members of the godly realm.general understanding of origin of Ba Jia Jiang is derived from the existence of eight generals who performed exorcism of evil spirits for the Wufu Emperor (五福大帝). These eight generals became revered as gods of the underworld, represented as bodyguards or attendants for temples of nether Gods such as Dongyue Emperor (東獄大帝), Yama (King of Hell, 閻羅王) and Cheng Huang (the City Gods, 城隍). Gradually Ba Jia Jiang evolved to appear also as bodyguards to Wang Ye (Royal Lord, 王爺) and Matsu (媽祖), and at many other temples. Later on, believers at temples dressed up as Ba Jia Jiang in to defend the Gods. These actions evolved into Taiwanese folk activities, part of Wu Array (Military Array, 武陣) in Din Tao (Taiwanese troupes, 陣頭). Ba Jia Jiang is responsible for capture of ghosts and evil spirits, bringing safety and good luck, and providing protection. They contain a strong religious nature, and Din Tao (Taiwanese troupes, 陣頭) often seem as mysterious, threatening and serious. Some Ba Jia Jiang members have relations with Taiwanese gangsters.
 Nightmarchers: In Hawaiian legend, Nightmarchers ("huaka'i pō" or "Spirit Ranks," " 'oi'o") are ghosts of ancient Hawaiian warriors. On nights of Kane, Ku, Lono, or on nights of Kanaloa they said to come forth from burial sites to march out to past battles or to other sacred places. They march at sunset and just before sun rises. Anyone living near their path may hear chanting and marching, must go inside to avoid notice. They might appear during the day if coming to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.Anyone looking upon or seen by marchers will die unless a relative is within the marchers' ranks- some people maintain if you lie face down on the ground they will not see you. This is to show respect. However, if exiting area is fastest option, it is recommended. Placing leaves of the ti ("Cordyline" sp.) around one's home said to keep away all evil spirits, and will cause huaka'i pō to avoid the area. Another thing to always highly respect night marchers which can result in great things.

Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette: Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette (] ; 6 September 1757 – 20 May 1834), in United States often known simply as Lafayette, was a French aristocrat and military officer fought in American Revolutionary War. close friend of George Washington, Alexander Hamilton, Thomas Jefferson, Lafayette key figure in French Revolution of 1789 and July Revolution of 1830.
 The Cellar (Enfield, North Carolina): The Cellar is historic home at Enfield, Halifax County, North Carolina. dates to early-19th century large two-story, five bay, frame dwelling with attached one-story kitchen exterior brick end chimneys steep gable roof. childhood home of Congressman and Confederate General Lawrence O'Bryan Branch (1820-1862). house visited by Marquis de Lafayette during grand tour.
 Bell-Sherrod House: Bell-Sherrod House is historic home at Enfield, Halifax County, North Carolina. built about 1859, two-story, rectangular, Italianate-style frame dwelling with Greek Revival-style front porch. shingled hip roof pierced by two interior chimneys sheathed in weatherboard. conservatory added about 1915. house restored about 1987.
 James H. Parker House: James H. Parker House is historic home at Enfield, Halifax County, North Carolina. built in 1882, two-story, three bay, Italianate-style frame dwelling side-gable roof with overhanging eaves features one-story porch with low-hipped roof supported by paired (tripled at corners) chamfered columns topped by built-up and scroll-sawn brackets. on property is contributing smokehouse (c. 1855, 1882).
Enfield, North Carolina: Enfield is a town in Halifax County, North Carolina founded in 1740. 2010 United States Census town’s population was 2,532 increase of almost 8% from population 2,347 at 2000 census oldest town in Halifax County once world’s largest raw peanut market. Enfield part of Roanoke Rapids, North Carolina Micropolitan Statistical Area.
 John Hamilton (American Revolution): John Hamilton (died December 12, 1816) was military officer in British Army commander of Royal North Carolina Regiment of Loyalist provincial volunteers during American Revolutionary War from 1777 to 1783. Prior to Revolution Hamilton successful merchant in Halifax, North Carolina with business interests throughout Province of North Carolina. Hamilton commanded soldiers in major engagements, including battles of Briar Creek, Camden, Guilford Courthouse, Yorktown. After conclusion of war Hamilton made British consul to Norfolk, Virginia, one of only three Loyalists to receive consular positions in newly created United States.

Colt McCoy: Daniel "Colt" McCoy (born September 5, 1986) is American football quarterback for Washington Redskins National Football League (NFL). drafted by Cleveland Browns in third round of 2010 NFL Draft after playing college football for University of Texas. member of San Francisco 49ers.
 Case McCoy: Casey Burl "Case" McCoy (born February 12, 1990) former American football quarterback for University of Texas Longhorns football team. started 16 games for Texas over three-year period amassing 9–7 record. known as younger brother of NFL quarterback Colt McCoy.
 Walter Camp Award: Walter Camp Player of the Year Award given annually to collegiate American football player of the year decided by National Collegiate Athletic Association Division I FBS head coaches and sports information directors under Walter Camp Football Foundation; award named for Walter Camp, important influential figure in development of sport. Three players won award twice: Colt McCoy of University of Texas in 2008 and 2009, Archie Griffin of Ohio State in 1974 and 1975, O. J. Simpson of USC in 1967 and 1968.
 David Neill: David Neill (born July 17, 1980) American college football quarterback for University of Nevada from 1998 to 2001. In 1998, set NCAA record for most touchdown passes in a season by freshman with 29 thrown record tied in 2006 by Colt McCoy Texas Longhorns broken following season by Sam Bradford of Oklahoma. Neill previously held school record for most completed passes with 763 since broken by Cody Fajardo (878). received attention from Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Jets of NFL opted for veterinary career left football prior to 2002 NFL Draft.
 Sports team: sports team is group of individuals play sports, usually team sports, on same team. Historically, sports teams people play sports been amateurs., by 20th century, some sports teams and associated leagues became extremely valuable with net worth in millions. Real Madrid rated by Forbes as world most valuable sports team at $3.26 billion USD. Some individual sports have modified rules allow to be played by teams.
 1983 Stanley Cup Finals: 1983 Stanley Cup Finals contested by Edmonton Oilers first-ever Finals appearance and defending champion New York Islanders fourth, and fourth consecutive, Finals appearance. Islanders win best-of-seven series four games to none, to win fourth-straight and fourth-overall Stanley Cup. fourth straight Finals of post-1967 expansion teams, first involving former World Hockey Association (WHA) team. most recent time defending Stanley Cup champion won cup four years in a row, first (and to only) time North American professional sports team won four consecutive titles in any league competition with more than twenty teams. Since 1983, no professional sports team on continent win four straight championships and no NHL team won more than two consecutive championships (most recently Pittsburgh Penguins in ).

The Mighty Handful: (Russian: Могучая кучка ), also known as The Five and The New Russian School, were five prominent 19th-century Russian composers worked together to create distinctly Russian classical music. Mily Balakirev (the leader), César Cui, Modest Mussorgsky Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov Alexander Borodin lived in Saint Petersburg collaborated from 1856 to 1870.
 Alexander Borodin: Alexander Porfiryevich Borodin (Russian: Алекса́ндр Порфи́рьевич Бороди́н ; ], 12 November 183327 February 1887) was a Russian Romantic composer of Georgian origin, doctor and chemist. one of prominent 19th century composers known as The Mighty Handful, group dedicated to producing uniquely Russian classical music, than imitating earlier Western European models.

 Apratim Majumdar: (born 1978), Indian classical musician from Kolkata, India plays Sarod. His "Dhrupadee Veenkar" style of Ustad Alauddin Khan's Seni Veenkar Gharana imaginative prosodic progression melodic phrases technical brilliance maturity reminds legends of Gharana. internationally recognized instructor of classical Indian music.
 Sousaphone: sousaphone ( is brass instrument same family as tuba. Created around 1893 by J.W. Like tuba sound produced by moving air past lips vibrate or "buzz" into large cupped mouthpiece Unlike tuba instrument bent in circle to fit around body musician ends in large flaring bell pointed forward projecting sound ahead of player ease of carrying direction of sound widely employed in marching bands other musical genres.Sousaphones originally made brass mid-20th century started made lighter materials like fiberglass today both types wide use.

Berger Blanc Suisse: Berger Blanc Suisse (English: White Swiss Shepherd , German: "Weisser Schweizer Schäferhund" Italian: "Pastore Svizzero Bianco" ) is breed of dog from Switzerland. same origins as White Shepherd and German Shepherd Dog recognized as separate breed by FCI.
 Pandikona: Pandikona is primitive-type hunting dog from Pattikonda taluk-Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh state, India. "Pandikona medium size sight hound adapted to harsh climatic conditions of Kurnool district. breed associated with shepherd families region. PandiKona dogs need little care.
 Prosthetic Neuronal Memory Silicon Chips: Prosthetic Memory Chip is device imitates brain's process creating long-term memories device designed by Theodore Berger, Biomedical Engineer and Neurologist at University of Southern California. Berger started work on chip in early 1990s colleagues implant electrodes into rats and monkeys restore memories after impaired. researchers into developing memory prosthesis in animals need to show chips can form long-term memories in different behavioral situations. Berger hopes to use chips as electronic implants for humans brains suffer from diseases Alzheimer's disrupt neuronal networks.

Classical realism (international relations): is a theory of International Relations established post-World War II era to explain international politics as result of human nature. theory associated with thinkers Niccolò Machiavelli Thomas Hobbes. Modern thinkers associated with are Carl von Clausewitz, Hans Morgenthau Reinhold Niebuhr. Classical Realist thought overshadowed by Neorealism after Kenneth Waltz' work accepted due to rise of Structuralism in North American International Relations scholarship favored emphasis on rationality rather than human nature as cause for political conflict.
 On War: Vom Kriege (] ) is a book on war and military strategy by Prussian general Carl von Clausewitz (1780–1831), written mostly after Napoleonic wars between 1816 and 1830, published posthumously by his wife Marie von Brühl in 1832. translated into English several times as On War. "On War" is an unfinished work; Clausewitz revising accumulated manuscripts in 1827 did not to finish task. His wife edited his collected works published between 1832 and 1835. His 10-volume collected works contain most of his larger historical and theoretical writings, not shorter articles and papers or extensive correspondence with important political, military intellectual cultural leaders in Prussian state. "On War" formed by first three volumes represents his theoretical explorations. one of most important treatises on political-military analysis and strategy ever written, remains controversial and influence on strategic thinking.

Hawker Hurricane British single-seat fighter aircraft of 1930s–1940s designed built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd for Royal Air Force (RAF). overshadowed by Supermarine Spitfire aircraft renowned during Battle of Britain for 60 percent of RAF air victories served in major theatres of Second World War.
 No. 1455 Flight RAF formed at RAF Tangmere, West Sussex 7 July 1941 equipped with Turbinlite Douglas Boston Douglas Havoc aircraft co-operated with Hawker Hurricanes of 1 Squadron and 3 Squadron replaced with 534 Squadron on 2 September 1942
 Battle of Britain Memorial Flight Royal Air Force flight aerial display group comprising Avro Lancaster, Supermarine Spitfire Hawker Hurricane aircraft regularly seen at events Second World War British State occasions Trooping the Colour Queen Elizabeth II's 80th birthday 2006, wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge Catherine Middleton 2011 air displays throughout United Kingdom Europe

The Real Thing (Norwegian band): The Real Thing (1992-1995) was a Soul Jazz Band from Oslo, Norway, founded in 1992 when Sigurd Køhn and Palle Wagnberg formed forerunner, The B3 Blues Band with Vidar Busk and Hamlet Pedersen. changed name when Staffan William-Olsson and Fredrik Carl Stormer joined band. Størmer replaced by Torstein Ellingsen in 1995, and Ellingsen again by Børre Dalhaug in 1998. Due to sudden death of band's saxophonist Sigurd Køhn in December 2004 The Real Thing was hibernating until reunion in 2010.
 Torstein Ellingsen: Torstein Ellingsen (born 7 August 1966) is a Norwegian drummer and music producer, known from series of album recordings.
 Norwegians: Norwegians (Norwegian: "nordmenn" ) are a Germanic ethnic group native to Norway. They share common culture and speak Norwegian language. Norwegian people and their descendants are found in migrant communities worldwide, notably in United States, Canada, Australia, Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Brazil, Mexico, New Zealand, United Kingdom and South Africa.
 Turkish people: Turkish people (Turkish: "Türk ulusu" ), or Turks (Turkish: "Türkler" ), also known as Anatolian Turks (Turkish: "Anadolu Türkleri" ), are a Turkic ethnic group and nation living mainly in Turkey and speaking Turkish, the most widely spoken Turkic language. They largest ethnic group in Turkey, by far largest ethnic group among speakers of Turkic languages. Ethnic Turkish minorities exist in former lands of Ottoman Empire. In Turkish diaspora has established with modern migration, particularly in Western Europe.

Sasanian Empire: Sasanian Empire ( also known as Sassanian, Sasanid, Sassanid or Neo-Persian Empire known inhabitants as Ērānshahr in Middle Persian last period of Persian Empire (Iran) before rise Islam named after House of Sasan ruled from 224 to 651 AD. Sasanian Empire succeeded Parthian Empire recognised as of leading world powers alongside Roman-Byzantine Empire for more than 400 years.
 Farrukhzad Khosrow V: Farrukhzad Khosrau V was briefly king of Sasanian Empire from March 631 to April 631. son of Khosrau II.
 Samo: Samo founded first recorded political union of Slavic tribes known as Samo's Empire "tribal union"), from Silesia to present-day Slovenia ruling from 623 until death in 658. According to Fredegarius Samo was Frankish merchant unified Slavic tribes against robber raids violence by Avars bravery command skills in battle elected as "Slavic king" (Latin: "Rex Sclavorum" ). In 631 Samo defended realm against Frankish Kingdom in three-day Battle of Wogastisburg.

Stone Brewing Co.: Stone is brewery headquartered in Escondido, California, USA Founded in 1996 in San Marcos, California largest brewery in Southern California. 2016 sales volume ninth largest craft brewery in United States.
 Beer Wars: Beer Wars is 2009 documentary film about American beer industry. covers differences between large corporate breweries Anheuser-Busch Miller Brewing Company Coors Brewing Company opposed to smaller breweries like Dogfish Head Brewery, Moonshot 69, Yuengling Stone Brewing Co. other producers of craft beer. covered how advertising lobbyists to control beer market implying harm competition consumer choice.
 Microbrewery: microbrewery or craft brewery produces small amounts of beer (or sometimes root beer), smaller than large-scale corporate breweries independently owned. breweries characterized by emphasis on quality, flavour brewing technique.
 List of breweries in California: list breweries California current defunct includes microbreweries and larger industrial scale breweries. Brewing companies range widely in volume variety of beer produced from small breweries to massive multinational conglomerates. Since 1983, California allowed breweries to sell beer on premises rise to numerous brewpubs and microbreweries.

2016–17 Iona Gaels men's basketball team: 2016–17 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Gaels, led by seventh year head coach Tim Cluess, played their home games at the Hynes Athletic Center in New Rochelle, New York as members of the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC). They finished the season 22–13, 12–8 in MAAC play to finish in a tie for third place. They defeated Rider, Saint Peter's and Siena to be champions of the MAAC Tournament. They received the MAAC's automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament where they lost in the First Round to Oregon.
 2010–11 Iona Gaels men's basketball team: 2010–11 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. Gaels, led by first year head coach Tim Cluess, played their home games at Hynes Athletics Center and are members of the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference. finished the season 25–12, 13–5 in MAAC and lost in the championship game of the 2011 MAAC Men's Basketball Tournament to Saint Peter's. They were invited to the 2011 CollegeInsider.com Tournament where advanced to the championship game before falling to Santa Clara.

Russian Revolution: The Russian Revolution was a pair of revolutions in Russia in 1917 dismantled Tsarist autocracy led to rise of Soviet Union. Russian Empire collapsed with abdication of Emperor Nicholas II old regime replaced by provisional government during first revolution of February 1917 (March in Gregorian calendar; older Julian calendar was in use in Russia at time). Alongside it arose grassroots community assemblies (called 'soviets') contended for authority. In second revolution that October, Provisional Government was toppled all power given to soviets.
 Russia–United Kingdom relations: Russia–United Kingdom relations (Russian: Российско-британские отношения ) is relationship between Russian Federation and United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and it's overseas territories. Spanning nearly five centuries, it often switched from state of alliance to rivalry or even war. Russians and British were allies against Napoleon, enemies in Crimean War of 1850s, rivals in Great Game for control of central Asia in late 19th century. were allies again in World Wars I and II, relations strained by Russian Revolution of 1917. were at sword's point during Cold War (1947–91). Russian big businesses had strong connections with City of London and British corporations during late 1990s and 2000s.

Castle Air Force Base: Castle Air Force Base (1941–1995) is former United States Air Force Strategic Air Command base northeast of Atwater northwest of Merced 115 miles (185 km) south of Sacramento, California.
 Sierra Academy of Aeronautics: Sierra Academy of Aeronautics is aviation flight school in Atwater, California operates training facility at former Castle Air Force Base in Atwater, California. Sierra Academy contracted by several foreign air carriers perform pilot training, including Shanghai Airlines.
 ATP Flight School: ATP Flight School headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, largest flight training company in United States. privately held company founded in Atlanta, GA by current management small group of airline pilots in 1984. ATP’s initial focus was providing flight training to U.S. military pilots seeking Airline Transport Pilot Certificates to transition to commercial air carrier operations. focus on professional flight training ATP later expanded course offerings to include ab-initio training programs for domestic and international students seeking career in commercial aviation Today ATP leading supplier of professionally trained pilots to nation's regional airlines.

Baraki Barak: Baraki Barak is a town and center of Baraki Barak District, Logar Province, Afghanistan. It was also the former capital of Logar Province. town is in a mountainous area in the valley of the Logar River. The main road Ghazni-Kabul passes about 20 km to the West of town.
 Baraki Rajan: Baraki Rajan (Dari/Pashtun: برکی راجان) is a town within the Baraki Barak District of Logar Province, Afghanistan. Baraki Rajan lies approximately 3 km south of the town of Baraki Barak, the capital of Baraki Barak District. Baraki Rajan is the location of largest bazaar in the Baraki Barak District, with over 1,200 shops and businesses, with a 50+ bed hospital near town center, making Baraki Rajan an important center for commerce within District.
 Baraki Barak airstrike: The Baraki Barak airstrike was a coalition airstrike occurred on August 26, 2011 in Eastern Afghanistan. Six Afghan civilians from the same family were killed in air strike in Baraki Barak district of Logar province, Afghanistan. Four insurgents and three Afghan army members were also killed.
 Logar Province: Logar (Pashto: لوګر ; Dari: لوگَر ) is one of the 34 provinces of Afghanistan, located in the eastern section of the country. is divided into seven districts and contains hundreds of villages. Puli Alam is the capital of the province.

Crescent Range: Randolph Mountains located in White Mountains of New Hampshire United States highest peak is Black Crescent Mountain elevation 3264 ft .
 Mount Crescent: Mount Crescent mountain in Crescent Range of White Mountains Randolph, New Hampshire 3,251 ft (991 m) high summit second highest mountain summit in Randolph after Black Crescent Mountain (3,264 feet, 995 m). Both mountains in Randolph's Ice Gulch Town Forest. 1896 topographic map Mount Crescent shown as "Randolph Mtn." elevation 3,280 ft, Black Crescent "Mt. Crescent" elevation 3,322 ft.
 Black Crescent Mountain mountain in Crescent Range of White Mountains 4.4 mi north of Randolph 4.7 mi southwest of Berlin New Hampshire summit on eastern boundary of White Mountain National Forest.
 Santa Cruz (Santiago): Santa Cruz town in eastern part of island of Santiago, Cape Verde 2 kilometers southeast from municipal seat of Santa Cruz Pedra Badejo on road linking Praia and Tarrafal through Pedra Badejo EN1-ST02. over 30 km NNW of Praia. 2010 population was 2,019. Santa Cruz part of Pedra Badejo area about 20,000 people as of 2010. Santa Cruz's population top 20 and top 25 populated places of island larger than oldest city Cidade Velha fourth most populated place in municipality as of 2010.

Stuart Roosa Stuart Allen "Stu" Roosa (August 16, 1933 – December 12, 1994), (Col, USAF), American aeronautical engineer, United States Air Force pilot test pilot NASA astronaut Command Module Pilot for Apollo 14 mission mission lasted January 31 to February 9, 1971 third mission to land astronauts (Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell) on Moon Shepard and Mitchell spent two days on lunar surface Roosa conducted experiments from orbit in Command Module "Kitty Hawk". one of 24 people to travel to Moon.
 Moon tree: Moon trees grown from 500 seeds taken Moon by Stuart Roosa Apollo 14 mission 1971 Command Module Pilot former smoke jumper Roosa contacted by Ed Cliff Chief of Forest Service proposed idea taking seeds along Seeds chosen from five trees: Loblolly Pine, Sycamore Sweetgum Redwood Douglas Fir.
 Apollo 16: tenth manned mission in United States Apollo space program fifth and penultimate to land on Moon first to land in lunar highlands second of "J missions crewed by Commander John Young, Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly Launched from Kennedy Space Center Florida 12:54 PM EST April 16, 1972 mission lasted 11 days, 1 hour, 51 minutes concluded 2:45 PM EST April 27.

Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. (film): Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. is an American television film based on the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury. first broadcast on May 26, 1998 on Fox. Directed by Rod Hardy, film stars David Hasselhoff as Fury, a retired super spy approached to return to duty to take down the terrorist organization HYDRA, who threaten to attack Manhattan with a pathogen reconstituted known as the Death's Head virus. Lisa Rinna plays Contessa Valentina "Val" Allegra de Fontaine, and Sandra Hess plays Andrea von Strucker / Viper. released on DVD on September 30, 2008.
 Nick Fury (2017 comic book): Nick Fury is a 2017 ongoing comic book series published by Marvel Comics. series is written by James Dale Robinson and primarily drawn by ACO. is the first series to feature Nick Fury Jr. as its main character.

College Humor (film): College Humor is a 1933 American pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Wesley Ruggles starring Bing Crosby, Jack Oakie, Richard Arlen Mary Kornman Mary Carlisle. Based on story by Dean Fales film about college professor and school's star football player become rivals for same beautiful coed. Released by Paramount Pictures, film co-stars George Burns Gracie Allen.
 Going Hollywood: Going Hollywood is 1933 American pre-Code musical film directed by Raoul Walsh starring Marion Davies Bing Crosby. written by Donald Ogden Stewart based on story by Frances Marion. "Going Hollywood" released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer on December 22, 1933.

Fred C. Koch: Fred Chase Koch ( ; September 23, 1900 – November 17, 1967) was an American chemical engineer and entrepreneur founded the oil refinery firm later became Koch Industries, a privately held company, under principal ownership and leadership of Koch's sons, Charles and David, is listed by "Forbes," as of 2015, as the second-largest privately held company in the United States.
 Koch family foundations: The Koch family foundations are a group of charitable foundations in the United States associated with the family of Fred C. Koch. The most prominent of are the Charles Koch Foundation and the David H. Koch Charitable Foundation, created by Charles Koch and David Koch, two sons of Fred C. Koch who own the majority of Koch Industries, an oil, gas, paper, and chemical conglomerate is the US's second-largest privately held company. Charles' and David's foundations have provided millions of dollars to variety of organizations, including libertarian and conservative think tanks. Areas of funding include think tanks, political advocacy, climate change scepticism, higher education scholarships, cancer research, arts, and science.

New York State Route 9R: (NY) is north–south state highway in northeastern Albany County, New York United States route is 3.22 mi eastern loop of U.S. Route 9 (US 9) connecting to city of Cohoes 1.5 mi east leaves US 9 in hamlet Latham rejoins parent in hamlet Boght Corners both in town of Colonie. Most NY 9R two-lane highway through residential areas southwesternmost portion four lanes wide serves commercial district route assigned c. 1939 largely unchanged since save for brief period during 1970s NY 9R partially replaced by NY 470.
 Boght Corners, New York: Boght Corners (also referred Boght) is hamlet in town Colonie northern Albany County, New York straddles U.S. Route 9 (Route corners at intersection of Route 9 and Boght Road (NY Route 9R east of hamlet), near Boght Community Fire District’s station community served by North Colonie Central School District. Boght Hills Elementary School within hamlet.
 New York State Route 9N: 9N (NY 9N) is north–south state highway in northeastern New York extends from intersection with U.S. Route 9 (US 9), NY 29, NY 50 in Saratoga Springs to junction with US 9 and NY 22 in Clinton County hamlet of Keeseville. 143.49 mi total length NY 9N is longest letter-suffixed route in state concurrent with parent route for 1 mi in village of Lake George three blocks in hamlet of Elizabethtown.

12 Years a Slave (score): 12 Years original soundtrack album to 2013 film "12 Years Slave" starring Chiwetel Ejiofor, Michael Fassbender Benedict Cumberbatch Paul Dano Lupita Nyong'o record contains twenty-one tracks from original film score written composed by Hans Zimmer. score admired contender for Academy Award for Original Music Score at 86th Academy Awards.
 Chiwetel Ejiofor: Chiwetel Umeadi Ejiofor, CBE ( born 10 July 1977) British actor. enrolling at National Youth Theatre in 1995 gaining scholarship to London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art at age 19 three months into course Ejiofor cast by Steven Spielberg play supporting role in film "Amistad" (1997) as James Covey.

Taj Mahal Bangladesh (Bengali তাজ মহল বাংলাদেশ )is scaled copy of original Taj Mahal Mughal mausoleum in Agra, India) 10 miles east of Bangladeshi capital Dhaka in Sonargaon. Unlike original work building took five years. Ahsanullah Moni, wealthy Bangladeshi film-maker announced 'Copycat version of Taj Mahal' project December 2008. project cost USD$56 Million built 20 miles northeast of Capital Dhaka Moni explained built replica of Taj Mahal poor nation realise dream of seeing India's famed monument. caused complaints from Indian officials can't copy historical monuments" official Indian High Commission in Dhaka told press.
 Agra Fort: Agra Fort is historical fort in Agra India main residence of emperors Mughal Dynasty till 1638 capital shifted from Agra to Delhi. Agra fort UNESCO World Heritage site 2.5 km northwest of famous sister monument Taj Mahal fort described as walled city.

Franco Corelli: Franco Corelli (8 April 1921 – 29 October 2003) was an Italian tenor had major international opera career between 1951 and 1976. Associated in with spinto and dramatic tenor roles of Italian repertory, he was celebrated universally for his powerhouse voice, electrifying top notes, clear timbre, passionate singing and remarkable performances. Dubbed the "Prince of tenors", Corelli possessed handsome features and charismatic stage presence endeared him to audiences. had long fruitful partnership with Metropolitan Opera in New York City between 1961 and 1975. appeared on stages of most of major opera houses in Europe and with opera companies throughout North America.
 Tosca (1956 film): Tosca is a 1956 Italian musical film directed by Carmine Gallone starring Franca Duval, Afro Poli and Franco Corelli. based on opera "Tosca" by Giacomo Puccini. made at Cinecittà in Rome.
 La Bohème (1988 film): La bohème (also known as "La bohème de Puccini") is a 1988 Italian-French film of an opera directed by Luigi Comencini. based on Giacomo Puccini's "La bohème".

New Orleans Pelicans: New Pelicans American professional basketball team in New Orleans, Louisiana Pelicans compete in National Basketball Association (NBA) member club league Western Conference Southwest Division. team plays home games in Smoothie King Center (formerly known New Orleans Arena).
 Jalen Jones: (born May 27, 1993) American professional basketball player for New Orleans Pelicans National Basketball Association (NBA). signed two-way contract with NBA G League played college basketball for Southern Methodist Texas A&M.
 Portland Trail Blazers: Portland Trail known Blazers American professional basketball team Portland, Oregon. Trail compete National Basketball Association (NBA) member club league Western Conference Northwest Division. team played home games in Memorial Coliseum before moving to Moda Center in 1995 (called Rose Garden until 2013) franchise entered league as expansion team in 1970 enjoyed strong following from 1977 through 1995 team sold out 814 consecutive home games longest streak in American major professional sports surpassed by Boston Red Sox. Trail Blazers only NBA team based in bi-national Pacific Northwest after Vancouver Grizzlies relocated to Memphis became Memphis Grizzlies in 2001, Seattle SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City became Oklahoma City Thunder in 2008.

Blues Traveler: Blues Traveler is an American rock band formed in Princeton, New Jersey in 1987. band's music covers variety of genres, including blues rock, psychedelic rock, folk rock, soul, Southern rock known for extensive use of segues in live performances, considered key part of re-emerging jam band scene of 1990s, spearheading H.O.R.D.E. touring music festival.
 Bridge (Blues Traveler album): Bridge is sixth album by American jam band Blues Traveler, released May 2001 (see 2001 in music). Blues Traveler's first album following 1999 death of bassist Bobby Sheehan. album originally titled "Bridge Out of Brooklyn."
 Blues Traveler (album): Blues Traveler, eponymous debut album from Blues Traveler, released on A&M Records in 1990. establishes band's trademark jam band sound featuring John Popper's harmonica.

Kinnaird Castle, Brechin: Kinnaird Castle is 15th-century castle in Angus, Scotland castle home to Carnegie family, Earl of Southesk, for more 600 years.
 Lady Charlotte Elliot: Lady Charlotte Elliot (22 July 1839 – 15 January 1880), born Charlotte Carnegie, Victorian poet born 22 July 1839 in parish of Farnell, Angus (possibly at Kinnaird Castle), Scotland.
 Fra Lippo Lippi (poem): Fra Lippo Lippi 1855 dramatic monologue by Victorian poet Robert Browning first appeared in collection "Men and Women". poem Browning depicts 15th-century real-life painter, Filippo Lippi. poem asks question whether art true to life or idealized image of life poem written in blank verse, non-rhyming iambic pentameter.

Battle of Berlin: The Battle of Berlin, designated the Berlin Strategic Offensive Operation by Soviet Union, was final major offensive of European theatre of World War II.
 Alexander Nikolayev: Alexander Petrovich Nikolayev (Russian: Александр Петрович Николаев; 14 November 1918 – 13 June 2009) was a Red Army senior lieutenant and Hero of the Soviet Union. He received title Hero of the Soviet Union and Order of Lenin for his actions during Battle of Berlin. Nikolayev also fought in Siege of Leningrad.
 Mikhail Linnik: Mikhail Nikiforovich Linnik (Russian: Михаил Никифорович Линник; 25 October 1916 – 21 December 2007) was a Soviet Army captain and Hero of Soviet Union. Linnik was awarded title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for actions during Lublin–Brest Offensive in September 1944.
 Georgy Vasilyevich Ivanov: Georgy Vasilyevich Ivanov (Russian: Георгий Васильевич Иванов; 25 May 1901 – 25 December 2001) was a Soviet Army major general and Hero of the Soviet Union. Ivanov was awarded title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for leadership of 6th Guards Rifle Division from late 1944 to 1945. Ivanov fought in World War II at Battle of the Dnieper and Vistula–Oder Offensive.

Cale Gundy: Joseph Cale Gundy (born April 10, 1972) is a former American football quarterback who played for Oklahoma Sooners from 1990 to 1993. While at Oklahoma he was a member of Delta Tau Delta International Fraternity. After coaching running backs for 16 years at Oklahoma Gundy was promoted to Assistant Head Coach and moved to Inside Receivers for the 2015 season. His brother, Mike, is the head football coach at Oklahoma State University.
 Mike Gundy: Mike Gundy (born August 12, 1967) is an American football coach and former player. He is currently the head football coach at Oklahoma State University. Gundy played college football at Oklahoma State, he played quarterback from 1986 to 1989. He became Oklahoma State's coach on January 3, 2005. In 2007, he received national media attention for his heated criticism of a newspaper article on one of his players.
 Ike Mahoney: Frank John Mahoney Jr. (October 25, 1901 – November 21, 1961) was an American football back who played five seasons with the Chicago Cardinals of the National Football League. He played college football at Creighton University and attended the Omaha High School of Commerce in Omaha, Nebraska. He was a member of the Chicago Cardinals team were NFL champions in 1925. He also played baseball, basketball and participated in track and field. Mahoney played for Chicago Bruins of the American Basketball League. He had received an offer to play baseball for Pittsburgh Pirates but opted to play football for Chicago Cardinals.

Bayezid II Mosque (Amasya): is historical 15th century Mosque in Amasya, Turkey. built in 1486 by order of Ottoman sultan Bayezid II largest Külliye of city.
 Beyazıt Square: Beyazıt Square (Turkish: "Beyazıt Meydanı" ) is square in district of Fatih, in European part of Istanbul, Turkey. officially named "Freedom Square" ("Hürriyet Meydanı" ), known as Beyazıt Square after Bayezid II Mosque one side Square former site of Forum of Theodosius built by Constantine the Great. one side is main entrance of Istanbul University; Beyazıt Tower on university's campus seen from square. current form square designed by Turgut Cansever.
 Gazi Atik Ali Pasha Mosque: Gazi Atik Pasha Mosque (Turkish: "Gazi Atik Ali Paşa Camii" ) is old Ottoman mosque in Çemberlitaş neighbourhood of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. construction started under orders future Grand Vizier Hadım Atik Ali Pasha in 1496 completed in 1497 during reign of Sultan Bayezid II. mosque near entrance to Kapalıçarşı (Grand Bazaar), Column of Constantine, historical Nuruosmaniye Mosque.

Greg Monroe: Gregory Keith Monroe Jr (born June 4, 1990) American professional basketball player for Milwaukee Bucks National Basketball Association (NBA). freshman season at Georgetown University Monroe named Big East Rookie of the Year. drafted by Detroit Pistons 2010 NBA draft seventh overall pick last Pistons player to wear #10 jersey after Pistons retired number for Dennis Rodman at halftime game against Chicago Bulls April 1, 2011.
 Jerome Williams (basketball): Jerome Williams (born May 10, 1973) American retired professional basketball player last played for New York Knicks NBA. star player on Magruder High School basketball team. Drafted Georgetown University by Detroit Pistons 26th pick of 1996 NBA Draft (the pick originally belonged to San Antonio Spurs went to Pistons in Dennis Rodman trade), played four-plus years with Pistons one of key reserves. fan favorite during days for Toronto Raptors due to tenacious efforts on court.
 Detroit Pistons: Detroit Pistons American professional basketball team based in Detroit, Michigan. Pistons compete in National Basketball Association (NBA) member club of league's Eastern Conference Central Division. team plays home games at Little Caesars Arena founded in Fort Wayne, Indiana as Fort Wayne (Zollner) Pistons in 1941 member of National Basketball League (NBL). Pistons joined Basketball Association of America (BAA) in 1948. 1949 NBL and BAA merged to become NBA Pistons became part of merged league Since moving to Detroit in 1957, Pistons won three NBA championships in 1989, 1990 and 2004.

Temple of Music: The Temple of Music was a concert hall and auditorium built for the Pan-American Exposition held in Buffalo, New York in 1901. U.S. President William McKinley was assassinated inside the building on September 6, 1901. structure, like most other buildings at exposition, was demolished when the fair ended.
 Pan-American Exposition: Pan-American Exposition was a World's Fair held in Buffalo, New York, United States, from May 1 through November 2, 1901. fair occupied 350 acre of land on the western edge of now Delaware Park, extending from Delaware Avenue to Elmwood Avenue and northward to Great Arrow Avenue. It remembered today primarily for the location of assassination of President William McKinley.
 Assassination of William McKinley: On September 6, 1901, William McKinley, the 25th President of the United States, was shot on the grounds of Pan-American Exposition at Temple of Music in Buffalo, New York. He was shaking hands with public when Leon Czolgosz, an anarchist, shot him twice in the abdomen. McKinley died eight days later on September 14 of gangrene caused by gunshot wounds. He was the third American president to have been assassinated, following Abraham Lincoln in 1865 and James A. Garfield in 1881.
